article_blocks.text: Strain Type: Autoflowering hybrid
Genetics: AK-47 × White Russian × Diesel
Breeder: Short Stuff Seeds
THC Content: 15–18%
CBD Content: Low
Terpene Profile: N/A
Primary Flavors: Sweet fruit, diesel, earth, spice, skunk
Flowering Time (Indoor): 9–10 weeks from seed
Outdoor Harvest Time: 9–10 weeks from germination
Indoor Yield: 30–90 grams per plant
Outdoor Yield: 30–90 grams per plant
Grow Difficulty: Easy to moderate

Onyx arrived during an important transition in autoflowering cannabis. Early autos had earned a reputation for being small, fast, and convenient, but many could not match conventional photoperiod marijuana in flower density or potency. Short Stuff Seeds approached the problem differently, using extensive selection to create what it called a “Next Generation” autoflower. Onyx became one of the breeder’s flagship examples: a medium-sized, vigorously branching plant that finishes in roughly ten weeks from seed while producing dense, resin-heavy buds with a surprisingly forceful effect. Its personality is equally removed from the mild stereotype once attached to autoflowering weed. Sweet fruit meets pungent Diesel, while an initially elevated head high develops into a strong, lingering body stone.
Genetics and Lineage

Onyx was developed by Short Stuff Seeds and breeder STITCH from a complex stabilized genetic population containing AK-47, White Russian, Diesel, and additional breeding material that was intentionally kept undisclosed. The breeder did not present the cultivar as a simple three-parent cross. Instead, preserved Short Stuff descriptions call it the result of an unusually large selection project in which numerous crosses were evaluated and refined before the final autoflowering population was released.

The recognizable parents nevertheless explain much of the finished flower. AK-47 contributes potency and a strong psychoactive foundation, while White Russian reinforces resin production and tight bud structure. Diesel introduces the pungent fuel-like aroma that cuts through the sweeter fruit qualities. Ruderalis-derived autoflowering genetics are present through the breeding program as well, allowing the plant to begin flowering according to age rather than requiring a seasonal change in day length. That combination helped make Onyx significantly larger and more productive than many first-generation autoflowers.

Because the name has since been reused, lineage matters when identifying the strain. A modern cultivar sold as Onyx by Connected Cannabis has entirely different genetics and should not be confused with the Short Stuff Seeds version covered here.
Effects and Experience

Onyx can begin with more cerebral energy than its compact autoflowering structure might lead someone to expect. The opening phase often brings a pronounced shift in mood, a slightly heightened awareness of music and conversation, and a euphoric mental quality that reflects the AK-47 and Diesel portions of the family tree. At moderate amounts, the high can remain engaging enough for music, gaming, casual socializing, or an evening spent unwinding without immediately becoming sleepy.

The balance changes as the experience matures. Physical relaxation becomes heavier, the limbs can begin to feel loose, and the mental stimulation gradually gives way to a slower, more settled state. Historical breeder material described the strain’s effect as exceptionally strong, and that reputation is one of the reasons Onyx stood out among early autoflowers. Larger servings are much more likely to produce a pronounced body stone and reduced motivation.

Potency depends on the individual crop. Although historical commercial listings frequently cite THC in roughly the mid-to-high teens, no universal breeder-certified percentage exists. Dry mouth, dry eyes, dizziness, impaired short-term memory, and anxiety are possible with excessive THC intake, particularly for inexperienced consumers.
Medical Benefits

The combination of initial mood elevation and later physical calm has made Onyx appealing to some medical marijuana consumers seeking an evening-oriented strain. The heavier portion of the experience may temporarily make muscular tension or general discomfort less intrusive, while its relaxing character can suit people who use cannabis when trying to unwind before bed. THC-dominant weed may also increase appetite in some consumers.

These traditional uses should not be interpreted as clinical evidence that Onyx treats chronic pain, insomnia, anxiety, depression, or another medical disorder. The cultivar itself has not been evaluated in controlled clinical trials, and chemical composition varies between plants and harvests. Medical consumers should rely on the laboratory analysis of the specific product whenever available and discuss cannabis use with a healthcare professional when prescription medication or significant medical conditions are involved.
Flavor Profile and Aroma

Fruit provides the sweeter side of Onyx, but Diesel prevents the profile from becoming simple or candy-like. Opening a cured flower can release ripe fruit alongside a strong pungent edge reminiscent of fuel, skunk, and fresh cannabis resin. Grinding the bud generally amplifies the sharper qualities, exposing earthy and mildly spicy notes beneath the initial sweetness.

Flavor follows the aroma closely. A sweet, fruity entry can transition into earth and spice before the Diesel genetics leave a more penetrating finish on the exhale. Some plants may emphasize fruit more heavily, while others express stronger fuel or skunk. That variation is understandable considering the complex breeding population behind the cultivar.

No reliable breeder-issued terpene laboratory profile survives for Onyx, so assigning one universal dominant terpene would create more certainty than the historical evidence supports. Phenotype, lighting, temperature, harvest maturity, drying, and storage can all reshape the aromatic chemistry of marijuana flower. What remains consistent in preserved breeder descriptions is the contrast between fruitiness and pronounced Diesel pungency.
Growing Information

Onyx was created specifically to move beyond the extremely small Lowryder-style autoflowers common during the early development of automatic cannabis. Mature plants generally reach about 50–100 centimeters and produce significantly more lateral branching than primitive autos. Rather than forming one miniature central cola, healthy plants can develop numerous flowering sites carrying compact, resin-coated buds.

Its defining cultivation feature is speed. The full life cycle generally lasts around 63–70 days from seed, meaning there is no separate vegetative period followed by a photoperiod-triggered flowering phase. Historical Short Stuff material commonly gives yields around 30–90 grams per plant, although production varies considerably with phenotype, available light, root development, and environment. Some preserved listings report substantially higher yields under optimized high-density indoor cultivation.

Dense flower structure comes partly from the White Russian influence, while vigorous branching contributes to overall production. Indoors, its moderate final height makes the plant manageable where vertical space is limited. Outdoors, the automatic flowering trait means growers are not restricted to a traditional September or October harvest date; plants mature according to age, assuming temperatures and sunlight are adequate during the approximately ten-week life cycle.
FAQ
Is Onyx an indica or sativa?

Onyx is an autoflowering indica/sativa hybrid rather than a pure example of either category. Its experience also reflects that balance, beginning with a noticeable cerebral high before becoming increasingly physically relaxing and heavy.
What are the genetics of Onyx?

The original Short Stuff Seeds Onyx contains AK-47, White Russian, Diesel, and additional secret genetics selected and stabilized by breeder STITCH. The breeder described the cultivar as the result of a large breeding and selection project rather than a straightforward three-way cross.
Is Onyx an autoflower strain?

Yes. Onyx was one of Short Stuff Seeds’ early “Next Generation” autoflowers. It begins flowering according to plant maturity rather than requiring the reduced daylight hours used to trigger conventional photoperiod marijuana.
How long does Onyx take from seed to harvest?

Most plants finish in roughly 9–10 weeks from seed, with approximately 63–70 days frequently cited in preserved breeder descriptions. Individual plants and environmental conditions can shift maturity slightly.
What does Onyx strain taste like?

Sweet fruit forms the opening flavor, followed by earth, spice, skunk, and a noticeable Diesel finish. The Diesel portion of the genetics gives the strain considerably more pungency than its fruity aroma initially suggests.
Final Thoughts on Onyx

Onyx deserves recognition not simply as another autoflowering weed strain but as part of the generation that helped change perceptions of what automatic cannabis could become. Short Stuff Seeds and STITCH combined AK-47, White Russian, Diesel, and additional carefully selected genetics to create a plant that retained automatic flowering while becoming taller, more branched, more resinous, and substantially more potent than many early autos.

Its sweet-fruit-and-Diesel profile, dense trichome-covered flowers, rapid ten-week life cycle, and progression from cerebral elevation into a heavier body stone give the cultivar a character that remains easy to distinguish. For cannabis enthusiasts interested in the development of modern autoflowering genetics, Onyx represents an important step between the tiny Lowryder era and the increasingly sophisticated auto marijuana strains that followed.
